source.title: SAEs Are Good for Steering - If You Select the Right Features
source.authors: Dana Arad; Aaron Mueller; Yonatan Belinkov

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features as objects for steering and builds a feature-selection method around them, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, feature recovery, or the geometry of feature representations.
record.gate_note: The study reports results about SAE feature scores and steering, not about whether sparse features are represented by overlapping directions or whether SAEs recover the model's complete or canonical units. Rows below capture the reported SAE-feature findings as related evidence; none measures a claim version. The AxBench comparator scores are reported from Wu et al. and are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study takes pretrained SAE features (Gemma Scope, Llama Scope, Pythia SAEs) as given and builds a feature-selection score for steering. It reports layer-wise input/output score patterns and steering success. It does not measure superposition geometry, capacity allocation, polysemanticity causes, whether SAEs recover real features, completeness or canonicality of SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Its results concern its own method's performance, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that features with high output scores steer far better than features with high input scores. They find the two roles rarely co-occur and sit at different depths. Output-score filtering makes SAE steering competitive with supervised methods on AxBench. They draw no conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pretrained SAEs, logit-lens-derived input/output scores, and feature steering on language models; it does not reproduce the original toy-network setup or its sparsity-dependent geometric measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering success changes with output-score filtering threshold and layer subset; feature score patterns differ by model. The study reports high correlation (0.9557) across neutral-prompt choices for output scores.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features split into input-aligned features (early layers) and output-aligned features (later layers), and high values of both scores rarely co-occur. Filtering by output score raises steering success 2–3x over unfiltered and random-filtered sets, including on AxBench (L20: 0.546 vs 0.293; L31: 0.470 vs 0.387).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLM residual-stream SAEs, a feature's causal output effect, more than its input activations, predicts its usefulness for steering. Input- and output-aligned roles are largely separate and depend on layer.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper studies residual-stream SAE features and single-feature steering, not the full range of model components or combinations of features. The main steering metric counts generated logit-lens tokens and perplexity is used for coherence; the authors note that feature interactions remain unstudied. AxBench evaluation uses an external LLM rater and separately sampled instructions from those used in the prior report; the authors note possible evaluation instability. Many plotted results have no exact numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted prior-work comparator results in Table 1 because they are reported from Wu et al. rather than measured in this study. Omitted individual qualitative steering examples in Figure 2 and Appendix Tables 2–4; they illustrate examples but do not provide a separate summarized metric result.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transition, and geometry: not studied.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity: not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity: not studied.
Whether SAEs recover real sparse features, or whether features are distributed across neurons: SAEs are assumed to work, not evaluated.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features: not evaluated. The input/output role split concerns steering usefulness, not canonicality.

record.verdict_notes: The Section 2.1 description of polysemanticity and SAEs is background citation only. The study is not an original source. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated versus shared dimensions by feature importance.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

Whether real-model features are distributed across neurons or whether SAE features recover such features; the study uses existing SAEs but does not assess recovery or feature distribution across neurons.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representation.
Whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured input and output scores for 100 randomly sampled SAE features per layer.
rows.measure: Input and output scores by layer
rows.value: Early layers (0–50% of depth) tend to have high input scores and near-zero output scores; later layers (66–100%) show near-zero input scores and increasing output scores; middle layers tend to score low on both.
rows.note: The study describes layer-wise score patterns, not superposition geometry.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1 8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured input and output scores for randomly sampled SAE features by layer.
rows.measure: Input and output scores by layer
rows.value: No early-layer trend was observed; around 50% depth, both scores become non-zero, with low input scores and increasingly growing output scores in later layers.
rows.note: The authors suggest early-layer logit-lens limitations as a possible explanation.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Measured input and output scores for sampled SAE features by layer.

conditions.value: 100 randomly sampled per layer with at least 10 recorded activations

rows.measure: Input and output scores by layer
rows.value: Output scores rise around 50% depth; input scores are mainly zero for most tested features.
rows.note: The authors suggest the model's smaller size may be related to this pattern.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Steered using SAE features retained by an output-score threshold.
rows.measure: Mean generation success@20
rows.value: figure only; the text reports an increase from around 0.5–0.6 without filtering to 1.1–1.4 at threshold 0.9 across both Gemma models, without mapping exact values to each model
rows.note: The paper reports the two-model ranges jointly; exact model-specific values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The value range (0.5–0.6 to 1.1–1.4) is reported jointly for both Gemma models, not for Gemma-2-2B alone. The random-filter control (no significant gain) should be noted as the comparison.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared output scores from the original neutral prompt with mean scores across 50 neutral prompts.
rows.measure: Correlation between original-prompt output score and mean output score
rows.baseline: original neutral prompt compared with the mean across prompts
rows.note: The authors interpret the correlation as showing little impact from the particular neutral prompt.
rows.check: This is a robustness check of the study's own output score (correlation 0.9557), not a finding about features. It is better treated as method_sensitivity than as a main result.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Examined the relationship between input and output scores across sampled SAE features.
rows.measure: Co-occurrence of high input and high output scores
rows.value: Most features lie near one score axis or the other; some features have both high input and high output scores.
rows.note: This concerns the study's score taxonomy, not whether model features overlap geometrically.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured pointwise mutual information between generated tokens and top-1 logit-lens tokens, grouped by input and output scores.

conditions.value: output score at least 0.1 and input score below 0.1; high input score groups

rows.measure: PMI of generated tokens with top-1 logit-lens tokens
rows.value: High-output, low-input-score features have negative PMI on average; high-input-score features have higher PMI regardless of output-score group.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 8 distributions shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: The authors associate negative PMI in the high-output, low-input group with repeated generation of the same token.
